• E-invoice transport: We accept PDF invoices via secure SFTP (preferred for now). We can accept Peppol/UBL if you plan to send structured invoices — please let me know and we will share our endpoint details.
• Bank/remit: I'll include a scanned bank instruction form for Redwood in the attachments; please add our beneficiary name exactly as provided to avoid rejections.

Laura — quick answers from Finance (copied from internal notes):

1) PO placement: header-only PO is acceptable. We'll add a reconciliation rule to match header PO -> invoice metadata. Please ask them to ensure the header field is labelled exactly "Purchase Order" in the PDF (case-sensitive for our OCR).

2) VAT/reverse-charge: since Oceanic Labs is GB VAT-registered, instruct them to issue invoices without UK VAT and include their VAT number plus a line stating "Reverse charge: UK VAT to be accounted for by the recipient under Art. 194 IVA/ VAT". We'll record the VAT number on their vendor record and our tax team will handle reverse-charge reporting. If they accidentally include VAT, we'll need a corrective credit note.

3) Required fields: invoice date, unique invoice number, supplier legal name, supplier VAT number, buyer PO (header), total net amount, currency, and bank details. GL code / Cost center are helpful but not mandatory; we can map via the PO.

4) Test invoice: approve sending a single PDF test to our SFTP. If they plan to use Peppol later, ask them to share participant ID and we'll onboard the endpoint.

I'll prepare a short checklist we can share with Oceanic (I can do it today).
